text:
matt: Heads-up — audit UX backlog item: we need a concrete plan for linking service/SSO actors to policy changes in exports. current NDJSON gives only `actor_id` which is ambiguous across identity sources.
anya: +1. Customers keep asking "who actually clicked deploy" vs "which service rotated the key". We need actor resolution levels.
devon: can we add `actor_type` (human|service|delegated) and `actor_handle` (display string) to the event payload? that'll make UI grouping easier.
eva: would prefer canonical `actor_principal` with source tag (okta, google, internal) so we can dedupe across directories.
matt: proposal: export schema has `actor_id`, `actor_principal`, `actor_source`, `actor_type`, `actor_resolution_level` (user|app|unknown). Also include `actor_hint_list` for fuzzy matches.
anya: sound ok. what's the perf hit for adding an additional 3 small string fields on hot path? we generate millions of audit events.
devon: negligible for producer side, main cost is enrichment lookups (calling identity service). we can do async enrichment with eventual consistency and mark events as `actor_enriched: true|false`.
eva: UI needs immediate display for console. If enrichment is async, add `actor_display_fallback` which is best-effort cached label.
matt: agree. And we should include `change_diff` small diff (compact list of {path, before, after}) not full objects — size concerns.
anya: +emoji: :thumbsup: compact diff helps search and reduces export bloat.
devon: on export format — customers asking for signed bundles (S3/Parquet) for compliance ingestion. NDJSON streaming is easiest for live consumers.
eva: suggested: default streaming NDJSON, add an optional monthly Parquet snapshot for heavy analytics. include schema version and signing metadata.
matt: rollout plan: add fields behind feature flag `audit_enriched_v2`, default off. canary to internal tenants first, then beta customers.
devon: API debate: should the enrichment be on write path (synchronous) or background worker? I vote background worker + tombstone events to indicate pending enrichment.
anya: background worker feels safer for latency SLAs. But then console must query enrichment store for latest actor labels when showing a trail — that's another surface.
eva: console change: UI will show "actor (resolving...)" and update via websocket when enrichment arrives. fallback to `actor_display_fallback` if none.
matt: export consumers who require immediate canonicalization can subscribe to a 'resolved-actors' topic — we'll publish enriched diffs there.
anya: about PII/redaction: we should let tenants opt into `actor_principal` export. default for hosted plans: mask email local-part, for enterprise opt-in full.
devon: note: masking should be reversible only via KMS-unseal for compliance teams. add `actor_principal_encrypted` with KMS tag for enterprise.
eva: telemetry: add a telemetry counter `audit.enrichment.latency` and `audit.export.size_bytes` and tie SLO alerts to them.
matt: also add rollout gating: if enrichment latency > 2s for 5m, disable enrichment writes and serve fallbacks.
anya: quick sample of NDJSON event we discussed:
{"ts":"2028-09-12T18:23:01Z","tenant_id":"t-123","actor_id":"u-853","actor_principal":"m***@example.com","actor_source":"okta","actor_type":"user","actor_enriched":false,"change_diff":[{"path":"/routing/policy/45/priority","before":"10","after":"20"}],"request_id":"r-999"}
devon: love it. last question: export retention/quotas — adding these fields increases export volume. ops wants a quota estimate.
eva: rough calc: enrichment fields add ~120 bytes per event, diff compacting saves ~200 bytes on median, net change ~-80 bytes for policy-changes but worst-case +500 bytes for big diffs.
matt: ops/infra: can you add a separate quota bucket `audit_bytes` so customers can see cost impact? tie to billing for hosted exports.
anya: I'll update the UX mockups for console trail with resolving state and export opt-in checkbox.
audit-bot: reminder: created Jira ticket AI-1423 "actor-enrichment-and-audit-export-v2" assigned to @devon, due in 2 weeks.
